sourceFindings.finding: Static local module imports and entry process metadata assertions precede launch(). CLI stdout/stderr publication is inside the admitted CLI, not a pre-admission outside capture owner.

Deadline begins inside launch, after CLI startup and entry checks. Existing owner and immediate handlers supervise the one inner controller; contain kills owner.handle (that controller), not the already-admitted outer CLI. Existing save/controller stdout/stderr capture is not outside-CLI startup raw capture.

Approved proposal explicitly delegates pre-admission ownership, bounded raw capture, startup-inclusive deadline and observed CLI termination to an external direct-exec owner, with no additional Node REPL/Node wrapper.

exposedToolGap: exec_command yield_time_ms is a return/poll interval, not an autonomous 300000ms process-tree containment/reap guarantee. max_output_tokens bounds rendered tool output tokens, not raw byte capture in an owned archive.

The exposed tool schema does not specify before-admission raw archive enrollment, combined raw byte counters/overflow containment, or whole-CLI close/cleanup evidence. Hidden implementation behavior was not assumed or probed.

A shell redirect could place raw bytes outside the CLI, but by itself does not establish the complete bounded deadline/overflow/descendant-retirement contract. No redirect/watchdog/ulimit recipe was substituted or trialed.

Using the existing Node REPL to retain a native spawn owner would add a third campaign Node process to the exact CLI+controller design; the approved profile forbids that extra wrapper. No such spawn occurred.

permissionFinding.qualification: Trusted outer mode is disclosed by the approved proposal. This audit does not relabel it an OS sandbox. If the current restriction instead demands enforced narrow outer filesystem grants, that also requires a separately authorized recipe change; no such flags are invented.
